claims.text: Equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr exhibits 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility.
Equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr has a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C.
Equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr has inadequate oxygen resistance for high-temperature applications.
The proposed intervention is to add approximately 2 at.% Al during casting.
A 2 at.% Al addition will produce a continuous Al2O3 scale on equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr at high temperature.
The resulting Al2O3 scale will be thin and adherent.
Al in the modified alloy will oxidize preferentially.
Preferential oxidation of Al will form a dense alumina layer.
The alumina layer will slow further oxygen penetration into the alloy.
Slower oxygen penetration will mitigate pesting.
The 2 at.% Al addition will not degrade useful room-temperature mechanical properties.
The 2 at.% Al addition will not degrade useful high-temperature mechanical properties.
Relative to untreated material, the Al-modified alloy will have a significantly lower oxidation rate during 5 hours in air at 800 °C.
Relative to untreated material, the Al-modified alloy will exhibit less scale spallation during 5 hours in air at 800 °C.
After the specified oxidation exposure, the Al-modified alloy will retain mechanical properties comparable to untreated material.
Aluminum has previously been used to improve oxidation resistance in related refractory alloys.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis requires both improved oxygen resistance and preserved mechanical performance, but the falsification rule requires both oxidation improvement to fail and mechanical-property retention to fail. Failure of either required outcome alone would contradict the hypothesis but would not satisfy the stated falsification rule.
